newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline hit by Japan seller.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline hit by Japan seller.

text.p: Gasoline prices fell under the pressure of aggressive selling, knocking Tuesday's firmer sentiment on emerging regional demand, traders said on Tuesday.
A Japanese trader lowered an offer for 50,000 barrels of 92-octane unleaded gasoline from $25.05 per barrel fob Singapore to trade with another Japanese trader at $24.50 late in the day.
Traders said the news of India's tender for two more cargoes of gasoline to the west coast to cover refinery maintenance, had now been factored into the market.
On Wednesday, traders said some of the 93-octane Chinese cargoes lifting in February may head towards India.
Market talk was dull although some supplies were still available from Singapore and Indonesia in February.
Naphtha prices eased with February swaps off 10 cents to $22.90/$23.20 per barrel.
On the physical market, a major was heard offering second-half February cargo of 0.66SG at 95 cents per barrel over Singapore quotes, fob Singapore.
Traders awarded the Indian naphtha tenders were heard shipping the three cargoes lifting end January/early February from Madras and Cochin to South Korea.
